title: Automate interview debrief summaries
description: A system that turns raw interviewer notes into a structured debrief keyed to your scorecard so every candidate gets compared the same way.

agent.title: Agent
agent.content: An AI that works independently to complete a goal — planning steps, picking tools, running them, and deciding what to do next without you prompting it at every step. Unlike a chatbot, an agent takes action.

model.title: Model
model.content: A specific trained version of an AI. Claude has several models (like Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) that differ in capability and speed. Larger models are smarter but slower; smaller ones are faster and cheaper.

skill.title: Skill
skill.content: A plain-text file with instructions for a specific repeatable workflow. Save it once, then trigger it with a slash command like /research-competitive. Same steps and output format every time — like a macro for Claude.

slack.title: Slack
slack.content: The team messaging app most companies run on. In Level 2, students connect Slack to their AI tools to trigger workflows from messages, post AI-generated updates to channels, or summarize threads automatically.

claude.title: Claude
claude.content: The AI made by Anthropic. Available as a chat tool at claude.ai, as a desktop app (Claude Desktop), and as a terminal tool (Claude Code). The different interfaces are suited for different types of work.

deploy.title: Deploy / Deployment
deploy.content: Taking code that works on your computer and making it live on a server so others can access it via the internet. When Claude 'deploys' a site, it's publishing it to the web.

notion.title: Notion
notion.content: An all-in-one workspace for docs, wikis, databases, and project tracking. Used heavily across the AI Builder program as a destination for AI-generated content and as a connected app in Level 2 automations.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.content: The instruction or message you give to an AI. The quality of your prompt directly shapes the quality of the output. Writing better prompts is one of the highest-leverage skills in this program.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.content: The written definition of what a good output looks like, in 3–5 scoreable dimensions. Evals grade against a rubric; without one, 'is this good?' is a vibe, not a measurement.

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
chatgpt.content: OpenAI's chat assistant. The most widely known AI tool — works similarly to Claude but with different strengths and weaknesses. Useful to have access to for cross-checking outputs or trying alternate models.

read-only.title: Read-only
read-only.content: The first rung of the trust gradient: the agent can see your inbox, calendar, or docs but can't change anything. The default starting state for every new tool connection. Tiny blast radius, fast to ship, and confirms the read side works before you graduate the write side.

tool-connectors.title: Tool Connectors
tool-connectors.content: Integrations that let Claude read from and write to apps you use (Gmail, Slack, Google Calendar, Notion, HubSpot, etc.). Set up once in Customize → Connectors. Each connector opens up a new category of tasks Claude can automate.

children.text: Every interviewer takes notes differently, typed, dictated, or dropped into an ATS field, and a hiring committee still has to compare candidates across all of it. [Gartner's May 2025 survey](https://hrexecutive.com/agentic-ai-in-hr-unpacking-the-hype-and-addressing-the-uncertainty/), as reported by HR Executive, found 82% of HR leaders plan to [deploy](#tooltip-deploy) some form of agentic AI within 12 months, including tools that structure and summarize hiring data. This system turns each interviewer's raw notes into a debrief mapped to the scorecard's competencies, so the committee reads one consistent format instead of five personal styles.

Unstructured notes make it hard to compare candidates fairly because each interviewer records different details in a different order. The debrief keeps the interviewer's own language for quotes and separates evidence from impression, so nothing becomes a rating no one gave.

Run it as a paste-in [prompt](#tooltip-prompt) after each interview, a saved skill, or a scheduled [agent](#tooltip-agent) that watches your ATS and posts debriefs to the hiring committee's channel. Every version stays [read-only](#tooltip-read-only) against your ATS.

Open your AI chat and have it interview you into a scope document. Done means a written scope naming how interviewers take notes, what a debrief has to cover, and how debriefs reach the hiring committee.

children.prompt: I want to build a system with my AI tool that turns raw interviewer notes into a structured, comparable debrief. Ask me questions, one at a time, about how interviewers currently take notes (typed doc, voice memo, ATS free-text field), what a good debrief needs to cover, how debriefs get shared with the rest of the hiring committee, and what's gone wrong with debriefs in the past. Then write it up as a scope document I can build from.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: the interview surfaces the format gaps you didn't know you had, and the scope document becomes the brief every debrief gets built against.

items: How interviewers capture notes today, typed, dictated, or dropped into an ATS field.
Whether debriefs need to sync into an ATS field automatically or just land in a shared doc.
Whether the hiring committee reviews debriefs before or during a live discussion.

children.text: Bring the scope document. Pressure-test it first by pasting it into a fresh session or a different [model](#tooltip-model) and asking it to poke holes. Then gather any access it calls for. Common [connectors](#tooltip-tool-connectors) are your ATS (Greenhouse, Lever, Workday), your note source (a shared doc or a voice-to-text app), and your hiring committee's shared space ([Slack](#tooltip-slack) or [Notion](#tooltip-notion)). The paste-in version needs none.
**Create.** Build and test the system on a real set of interview notes. The prompt below is one example; your scope document has the full version.

children.prompt:
Goal: Turn the raw interview notes below into a structured debrief for [candidate name], organized by the competencies on the scorecard for [role name].

Context: Raw notes: [paste/attach]. Scorecard competencies: [list]. Debrief format the hiring committee expects: [describe or link example].

Rules:
- Map every note to a specific competency; if a note doesn't clearly support any competency, put it in a separate "other observations" section instead of forcing a fit.
- Preserve the interviewer's actual language for direct quotes and flag anything that reads as a personal impression rather than a specific example.
- Never add a rating the interviewer didn't give.
- Output one debrief per candidate in the agreed format.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: mapping every note to a named competency forces the same structure onto five different note-taking styles, and the flag on personal impressions keeps opinion separate from evidence.

children.text: **Review.** Check the output against your scope. Every note mapped to a competency, quotes preserved, no invented ratings?
**Feedback.** Tell it exactly what went wrong (a quote filed under the wrong competency) and fold the correction into the rules.

items: Auto-flag when two interviewers' notes on the same candidate contradict each other.
Build a rolling summary across the whole panel instead of one debrief at a time.
Feed debrief language back into the scorecard build to see which questions produce useful notes.
Sync finished debriefs straight into your ATS candidate record.

children.text: **Measure** with a [rubric](#tooltip-rubric). Have your AI chat turn the scope bar into pass/fail checks and a run log in one pass.

children.prompt: From my scope document, write a rubric for judging each debrief, with 4 to 6 pass/fail checks. Then set up a simple run log I can keep in a doc or spreadsheet, with columns for candidate, interviewer, competencies fully covered, notes that didn't map to any competency, and what rule I changed. Give me both in a format I can paste into my notes.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: pass/fail checks remove the judgment call, and the log columns make recurring gaps visible after a run of candidates.

children.text: **Log** every run. Note the date, which rubric checks passed or failed, and what changed. A single miss is noise, and a repeated miss is an instruction you haven't written yet.

**Make skills** from what the log shows. Once the rubric passes a few candidates straight, package the prompt and corrected rules into a skill, so runs start from your defaults. A repeated failure earns its own skill. [Claude](#tooltip-claude)'s skill-creator skill will interview you and write it, and a custom GPT does the same in [ChatGPT](#tooltip-chatgpt).
One durable failure mode. It will smooth over vague or thin notes just as easily as strong ones, so a clean-looking debrief isn't proof the interview itself was rigorous.
